Deferred, not implemented. On the unmasked rolling mean and population std, Polars including conversion is slower than pandas at 2880 rows (3.2 ms vs 1.7 ms) and at 20000 rows (3.9 ms vs 5.0 ms), but 2.2x faster at 200000 rows on the compute node (0.017 s vs 0.038 s). The production masked path (where/ffill, train-only) was not ported or measured, and rolling_zscore_legacy_masked is 0.070 s at 200000 rows and outside the structure chain. Keep pandas until the masked path is measured.

deferred.reason: A first login-node measurement rejected this port: the zigzag loop was 25 ms of a 557 ms M1 structure chain at 20000 rows (about 4.6 percent). The compute-node run at 200000 rows changes that conclusion for the native path. There, detect_swings takes 0.239 s of the 0.502 s structure_levels native-backend call (about 48 percent), and about 8.7 percent of the python-backend chain (2.736 s). A Rust zigzag port could therefore roughly halve the native-backend structure_levels time. It is not implemented in this package, so no speed-up is claimed for it. Next step: implement behind the same explicit backend switch, run the same differential and property tests, and measure through the resource operator's spool.
